notes: DCA 6-2015 Table 3A, Dimension Lumber Deck Beam Spans (L_B) (p. 6; the document prints a second table designated 3A, joist hanger capacity, on p. 9, which is not this one), transcribed 2026-09-27 (#41 slice B2) from the PDF in the guide's sources, read from the page rendered at 300 dpi and checked against the text extraction; both agree on every cell. Rows carry the printed species group; each row's span is the L_B cell of its size row under the 'Joist Spans (L) Less Than or Equal to' column, an upper-bound band of the joist span L (the joist span as p. 3 defines it, face of support to face of support). A cell printed with two sizes ('3x8 or 2-2x8') is two rows, (1) 3x8 and (2) 2x8, citing the same cell. Members are written as napkin names a beam: plies and nominal size, '2-2x8' as (2) 2x8 and '3-2x8' as (3) 2x8. The joist span's domain min is napkin's smallest length (the table prints no lower bound); its max is the last column, 18'. Every note is transcribed verbatim and shown with results (not-encoded): notes 1 and 4 sit on the title's L_B and the Size heading, so apply to every row; notes 2 and 3 sit on species in the second group's heading, so ride on every row of that group. Table 3B (glued laminated timber, p. 7) is deliberately not transcribed. Not yet reviewed: docs/code-packs/reviews/us-ct-2022/dca6-table3a.md.

footnotes.text: Assumes 40 psf live load, 10 psf dead load, L/360 simple span beam deflection limit, cantilever length/180 deflection limit, No. 2 grade, and wet service conditions.
Incising assumed for Douglas Fir-Larch, Hem-Fir, and Spruce-Pine-Fir.
Design values based on northern species with no incising assumed.
Beam depth must be equal to or greater than joist depth if joist hangers are used (see Figure 6, Option 3).
